newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'shita Elec says weak yen boosts prft by Y150 bln.
newsitem.headline: M'shita Elec says weak yen boosts prft by Y150 bln.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co said on Thursday that the weak yen boosted its group profit by 150 billion yen in the last business year ended in March.
A company official also told a news conference that the Japanese consumer electronics giant assumed a dollar/yen rate of 115 yen in making its latest earnings estimates for the current business year.
The dollar stood at 116.10 yen in Tokyo at 0730 GMT.

Susumu Ishihara, a director, said Matsushita plans capital spending totalling 470 billion yen in 1997/98 on a group basis, up 13 percent from the year before, while its research and development spending is also expected to grow six percent to 460 billion yen.
The positive effect on its group profit from the weak yen, cost-cutting and robust sales was more than enough to offset the negative impact from falling sales prices, he added.
"In the (1996/97) business year, production and sales units at home and abroad performed steadily and group sales recorded its biggest ever level," he said.

Excluding the one-time effect from the company's sale of U.S. film maker MCA Inc, now named Universal Studios Inc, Matsushita's net profit would have grown by 28 percent in 1996/97, Matsushita said in a statement.
